newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom rise lifts German DAX to record close.
newsitem.headline: Telekom rise lifts German DAX to record close.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a solid start on Monday, as a surge in Deutsche Telekom AG helped the blue chip DAX index to a record closing high.
Surprising some dealers who had expected a more muted beginning, the 30-share DAX ended the bourse session up 12.96 points, or 0.36 percent, at 3,575.37 points.

Recently listed Deutsche Telekom, benefitting from interest ahead of its annual news conference on Tuesday and other factors, extended gains set Friday to set a new all-time high of 41.95 marks in early pre-bourse trade trade.
While the telecommunications giant pared its gains in bourse dealings, the stock still notched up gains of 1.24 marks, or 3.1 percent, to close at 41.19 marks.
Dealers said the weak dollar was having minimal impact on prices, as at around 1.69 marks it was still within an acceptable range.
"This shows a generally optimistic picture, especially for sectors like telecoms," said one dealer.

However others were more cautious, pointing out that volumes were in general rather weak. Deutsche Bank was one of the day's best performers, rising 2.35 marks to 95.10 marks, but dealers attributed this to technical factors.
Telekom's popularity was largely due to its upcoming news conference, at which it is expected to confirm glowing earnings expectations for the coming years.
Utility Veba AG, up 1.21 marks at 96.20 marks, was also benefiting from its involvement in telecommunications, dealers said.
Telekom's surge was partly because it is approaching a six-month deadline on May 19, after which its shares can be sold without incurring tax, dealers noted.
A report in Der Spiegel magazine that the company was planning marketing deals in commercial television in a bid to turn to profit on its cable business was also well received.
